{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Re-read the data with proper parsing of revenue
sales_df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue from string to float, handling thousands separators
sales_df['revenue'] = sales_df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Filter out refunded orders
sales_df = sales_df[sales_df['status'] == 'completed']

# Compute average revenue per order by channel, stratified by customer_segment
avg_revenue_by_channel_segment = sales_df.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['revenue'].mean().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Compute total number of orders per channel
order_count_by_channel = sales_df.groupby('channel').size()

# Compute overall average revenue per order by channel (weighted by segment)
# This adjusts for the differing segment composition
weighted_avg_revenue = (sales_df.groupby('channel').apply(
    lambda x: (x['revenue'] * x['customer_segment'].map(
        x.groupby('customer_segment').size().sum() / len(x)
    )).sum() / len(x)
)).round(2)

# Alternatively, compute properly weighted average by segment
# First, compute segment weights per channel
segment_weights = sales_df.groupby('channel')['customer_segment'].value_counts(normalize=True)

# Then, compute weighted average revenue per channel
weighted_avg_revenue = sales_df.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['revenue'].mean()
weighted_avg_revenue = weighted_avg_revenue.groupby('channel').apply(
    lambda x: (x * segment_weights[x.name]).sum()
).round(2)

# Show the results
weighted_avg_revenue"}
